etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Early Modern English dadd, dadde (circa 1500), undoubtedly older, from unrecorded Middle English *dadde, of uncertain ultimate origin.

definitions.definition: Used to address one's father; often capitalized
(slang) Used to address an older adult male

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From dade (“to strike heavily”), dade (“a heavy blow or thud”). Probably onomatopoeic.

definitions.definition: A blow; act of striking something.
(transitive) To throw against something; to dash.
Alternative form of daad (“Arabic letter ض”)
